docs.title: Overview
docs.text: ROS 2 tools to work with OSM data and perform path planning.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
This package parses a .gpx file with GPS waypoints into a Python class, queries OpenStreetMap for map features within the area, and serializes the result as a .mapdata file.

Parsed features are classified into three categories:

  • barriers — obstacles assumed to be untraversable (walls, buildings, fences, water…)
  • footways — paths intended for pedestrians
  • roads — areas intended for vehicles

Additional tools let you visualize the data, annotate it interactively, perform path planning, and publish a cost-aware footway point cloud for autonomous navigation.

The MapData class, the path planning modules, the create_mapdata CLI, and the interactive viewer work standalone without ROS 2 for data parsing, annotation, and planning. ROS 2 is required for osm_cloud, route_planner, and the viewer's live Tracker mode.

The package targets ROS 2 Jazzy or later on Ubuntu 24.04, and Python >= 3.12 for standalone use.

A sample GPX file and its .mapdata are in demo/ (buchlovice.gpx, buchlovice.mapdata).

docs.title: Standalone Python package (uv)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vras-robotour/map_data.git
cd map_data
uv sync
uv run python -m pytest

Alternatively, install as an editable package with pip:

pip install -e .

docs.title: With ROS 2 (colcon)
docs.text:
The map_data_interfaces package is nested inside this repository. Because colcon does not discover nested packages from a plain clone, run scripts/setup_ws.sh to create the workspace symlink before building:

# From your colcon workspace root (with this repo in src/map_data):
bash src/map_data/scripts/setup_ws.sh
colcon build --packages-up-to map_data
source install/setup.bash

ros2_numpy must be built from source

The ROS 2 nodes depend on ros2_numpy, which is not released as a binary package in any ROS distribution — rosdep install cannot resolve it. Clone its jazzy branch into your colcon workspace src/ and build it alongside this package.

map_data_viewer also wants simple-websocket (pip install simple-websocket), which rosdep cannot install; without it the browser polls over HTTP instead of a WebSocket (see Tracker).

To check the ROS 2 runtime nodes, run the smoke test script:

bash scripts/ros_smoke.sh

docs.title: Python library
docs.text: MapData and Way can be used directly in Python without a running ROS 2 node. The only requirement is that the package is installed (e.g. via pip install -e ., uv sync, or colcon build) so the parameters/ CSV files are accessible.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Parse a GPX file and save a .mapdata file:

from map_data.map_data import MapData

md = MapData("./demo/buchlovice.gpx")
md.run_all(save=True)  # queries OSM, parses, saves demo/buchlovice.mapdata

Load an existing .mapdata file and access parsed features:

from map_data.map_data import MapData

md = MapData.load("demo/buchlovice.mapdata")

print(len(md.roads_list))  # list of Way objects
print(len(md.footways_list))
print(len(md.barriers_list))

docs.title: Path planning
docs.text: The pathsolver module provides standalone planning capabilities — no ROS 2 context is required. Use the map_data_plan CLI to process waypoints against a .mapdata file, import the planners directly as a Python library, or run the route_planner ROS 2 action server.

docs.title: Offline route planning: map_data_plan and route_planner
docs.text:
The viewer's Planner screen (POST /api/create_replan), the map_data_plan command-line tool, and the route_planner ROS 2 action server all call map_data.pathsolver.route.plan_route on the same map data: the .mapdata file with its <stem>.annotations.json sidecar merged in (map_data.annotations.load_mapdata_with_annotations). Whatever is drawn, deleted, or split in the viewer is therefore reflected during planning.

Both tools support an explicit annotation choice: --annotations auto|none|FILE on the command line, or the annotations parameter on the node. none plans on the unedited OSM map, which is useful when an annotation store was pruned for another area.

Planner defaults come from config/planner_defaults.yaml (cell_size, inflate_obstacles, simplify_path, smooth_path, max_path_dist, grid_cost_weight). route_planner exposes the first four as ROS 2 parameters, re-read on every goal.

docs.title: Goal QR codes (Planner screen)
docs.text: Robotour provides goals as QR codes with a geo:lat,lon payload. In the Planner screen, right-click any waypoint and choose QR code, or press QR goal for the last waypoint: the code opens full screen on a white background (size slider) so a laptop or tablet can be held to the robot camera, with Download SVG (or PNG) for printing and Copy geo text for typing the goal in with qr_goal_send. The code comes from GET /api/qr.svg?lat=…&lon=…[&scale=12][&download=1][&caption=] as vector art, so it stays sharp at any size; GET /api/qr?… serves the same code as a PNG.

docs.title: Command line: map_data_plan
docs.text:
# Bundled demo map (the two waypoints of demo/buchlovice.gpx, ~420 m)
map_data_plan -f demo/buchlovice.mapdata --start 49.084416,17.336309 --goal 49.083106,17.338527

# Paths only (graph planner on footways), 3 m waypoint spacing, saved as a GPX track
map_data_plan -f coords.mapdata --start 50.1038,14.4294 --goal geo:50.1067,14.4193 \
    --spacing 3 --save route.gpx

# All-terrain (grid A*) through intermediate via points, printed as JSON
map_data_plan -f coords.mapdata -p 50.1038,14.4294 -p 50.1050,14.4250 -p 50.1067,14.4193 \
    --algorithm astar --cell-size 0.5 --json

docs.title: ROS 2 action server: route_planner
docs.text:
The route_planner node exposes an action server on /route_planner/plan_route (map_data_interfaces/action/PlanRoute).

ros2 launch map_data route_planner.launch.py mapdata_file:=coords.mapdata
ros2 launch map_data route_planner.launch.py mapdata_file:=coords.mapdata highway_types:=footway,road

ros2 action send_goal /route_planner/plan_route map_data_interfaces/action/PlanRoute \
    "{waypoints: [{latitude: 50.1067, longitude: 14.4193}], start_from_robot: true}"

docs.title: Goal execution, GPX saving, and waypoint spacing
docs.text:
• Cancellable goals: Action goals can be cancelled during execution. When cancelled, the action returns status CANCELLED and failure reason cancelled.
  • Boolean goal fields: Goal booleans (simplify_path, smooth_path) are evaluated as sent without falling back to node defaults.
  • save_gpx field:
    • Empty string (""): automatically writes a timestamped track to mission_dir/route_<timestamp>.gpx.
    • "-": disables GPX file output.
    • A .gpx file name: writes mission_dir/<name>. A path, .. or another suffix is refused (logged, nothing saved), since any host on the network can send goals.
  • spacing semantics:
    • spacing > 0: resamples the path so consecutive waypoints are at most spacing meters apart. Below 0.1 fails with bad_parameter.
    • spacing == 0: uses the node's default spacing (3.0 m).
    • Negative spacing (spacing < 0, e.g. -1.0): preserves raw planner vertices without densification.

docs.title: Action failure reasons
docs.text:
When route planning fails, PlanRoute.Result sets success = false and provides a machine-readable reason:

Reason Meaning bad_parameter Unknown algorithm or sub_algorithm, non-positive or non-finite cell_size, negative or non-finite inflate_obstacles, a positive spacing below 0.1 or infinite, or a waypoint UTM cannot express (latitude outside -80..84, non-finite) start_blocked Grid start coordinate lies inside an obstacle and cannot be snapped to free space goal_blocked Grid goal coordinate lies inside an obstacle and cannot be snapped to free space cancelled Planning request was cancelled busy Another plan is still running; the goal is not queued, send it again start_outside_map Start coordinate lies farther than outside_map_tolerance outside the map area goal_outside_map Goal coordinate lies farther than outside_map_tolerance outside the map area snap_too_far Waypoint exceeds maximum snap distance to the nearest allowed way unreachable Graph planner found no connection between endpoints in the way network no_path Grid planner found no collision-free path between endpoints grid_too_large Requested bounding area exceeds max_grid_cells route_too_long The route would have more than 200 000 waypoints (MAX_ROUTE_POINTS) too_few_points Fewer than two waypoints supplied without start_from_robot file_not_found Map data file could not be found or loaded; a goal's mapdata_file must be a relative name inside data_dir internal_error A bug in the planner; the node logs the traceback and keeps running no_fix start_from_robot requested but no recent GNSS fix was received on gps_fix_topic

docs.title: Python library usage
docs.text:
from map_data.annotations import load_mapdata_with_annotations
from map_data.pathsolver.route import RoutePlanningError, plan_route
from map_data.utils.gpx import create_gpx_track

md, _ = load_mapdata_with_annotations("demo/buchlovice.mapdata")
try:
    route = plan_route(md, [(49.084416, 17.336309), (49.083106, 17.338527)], spacing=3.0)
except RoutePlanningError as e:
    print(f"Planning failed ({e.reason}): {e.message}")
else:
    with open("route.gpx", "w") as f:
        f.write(create_gpx_track(route.latlon))

docs.title: Traversability rules
docs.text:
Which OSM ways the robot may drive on is decided from their tags by config/traversability.yaml, the single file to edit when routing rules change. The rules are applied when a map is loaded for planning (load_mapdata_with_annotations), ensuring that route_planner, osm_cloud, and intersection generation all observe the same network.

Keep traversability rules in sync between nodes

Both route_planner and osm_cloud must be configured with the same traversability file. If they differ, osm_cloud may publish intersection rings and cost clouds for ways that route_planner refuses to route over. route_planner detects rule file modifications automatically on each new goal, whereas osm_cloud reads the rule file once at startup and must be restarted after edits.

default:
  traversable: true
  cost: 0.0
rules:
  - match: {highway: steps}          # exact value
    traversable: false
    reason: stairs
  - match: {surface: [grass, mud, sand]}   # any of these values
    traversable: false
    reason: soft surface
  - match: {bridge: boardwalk}       # boardwalk bridges refused
    traversable: false
    reason: bridge
  - match: {smoothness: [bad, very_bad, horrible, very_horrible, impassable]}
    traversable: false
    reason: rough surface
  - match: {access: [no, private]}
    traversable: false
    reason: no access
  - match: {highway: path, informal: yes}   # multiple keys: all must match (AND)
    cost: 1.0
    reason: informal path
  • Rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins. A way that matches no rule receives default.
  • traversable: false removes the way: it is never routed over, its junctions receive no intersection rings, and it is excluded from osm_cloud.
  • cost: is optional and additive on top of highway/surface costs from config/planner_defaults.yaml: graph edge weights are (1 + way cost + rule cost) × length.
  • Rule and tag values are compared as strings (informal: yes matches informal: "yes").
  • Shipped defaults refuse stairs, soft surfaces (grass, mud, sand), boardwalk bridges (bridge: boardwalk), rough surfaces, and non-accessible ways.

docs.title: Graph planning
docs.text:
Plans a path by searching the OSM road and footway network using A*. The route is constrained to follow existing ways, making it suitable for on-road navigation. Its edge weights are length × (1 + way cost) using highway_costs/surface_costs tables plus any additive cost from traversability rules.

Walkable areas — closed area=yes (or multipolygon) ways such as pedestrian squares — are crossed directly rather than circumnavigated. The planner computes the shortest line-of-sight path within the polygon boundary between entry and exit points.

docs.title: Grid A*
docs.text: Discretizes the area around the route into a uniform grid and runs A* on it. Each cell carries a cost (see Cost grid); cells inside barrier polygons are impassable. Grid A* is complete (finds a path if one exists) and provides predictable runtime. Resolution and obstacle inflation are tuned via --cell-size and --inflate-obstacles.

docs.title: RRT*
docs.text: Rapidly-exploring Random Tree Star is a sampling-based planner that builds a tree of collision-free waypoints by randomly sampling the free space. RRT* is well suited for large open areas. If RRT* exceeds its iteration budget without finding a path, Grid A* runs on the same grid as a fallback.

docs.title: Cost grid
docs.text:
ReplanPath.fill_grid() converts OSM map data into a 2-D NumPy array of floating-point costs, one value per grid cell representing a cell_size × cell_size meter patch.

Cell cost assignment:

  1. Barrier polygons (inflated by inflate_obstacles, minus the ways of highway_types that cross them, such as a footway through a gate) are rasterized as impassable (cost = inf).
  2. For each remaining cell, the distance to the nearest way centerline is computed.

  3. If that distance is $\le$ max_path_dist, the cell receives a blended cost:

    $$\text{cost} = \text{way_cost} + (\text{default_off_path_cost} - \text{way_cost}) \times \left(\frac{\text{dist}}{\text{max_path_dist}}\right)^2$$

    where $\text{way_cost} = \min(\text{path_cost_cap}, \text{highway_cost} + \text{surface_cost})$.

  4. Cells beyond max_path_dist from any way receive default_off_path_cost (default 0.9).

Obstacle thresholds:

  • In Grid A*, only cells with cost inf (np.isinf) are treated as impassable obstacles. Cells with finite costs (even $\ge 1.0$) are traversable with weighted traversal cost.
  • In RRT*, cells with cost $\ge$ traversability_threshold (default 10.0) or inf are treated as obstacles.

docs.title: Grid resolution (cell_size)
docs.text:
cell_size is the dominant factor in memory consumption and planning time.

cell_size Grid cells per 100 m² Typical use case 0.5 m 400 Coarse survey, large open areas 0.25 m 1 600 Default — balanced resolution for pedestrian routes 0.1 m 10 000 Narrow gates, tight corridors

docs.title: Obstacle inflation (inflate_obstacles)
docs.text: Increasing inflate_obstacles adds a safety margin around barriers at the expense of potentially closing narrow corridors. If planning returns None, consider reducing this value.

docs.title: Path post-processing
docs.text:
• simplify_path (Douglas-Peucker) drops collinear and redundant vertices, reducing waypoint count without altering path geometry.
  • smooth_path applies gradient-descent smoothing to round sharp corners.

docs.title: Algorithm choice
docs.text: Situation Recommended algorithm Mapped pedestrian or road network, robot must stay on ways Graph planning Urban route with well-defined barrier obstacles Grid A* Large open area, sparse obstacles RRT*

docs.title: Using astar_search directly
docs.text:
astar_search is the generic A* implementation GraphPlanner uses (grid_astar has its own array-based loop). You can use it directly to build a custom planner for any graph-like problem.

from map_data.pathsolver.astar import astar_search


# Example: plan over a simple weighted grid
def neighbors(node):
    r, c = node
    candidates = [(r - 1, c), (r + 1, c), (r, c - 1), (r, c + 1)]
    return [(n, 1.0) for n in candidates if 0 <= n[0] < 10 and 0 <= n[1] < 10]


def heuristic(node):
    goal = (9, 9)
    return abs(node[0] - goal[0]) + abs(node[1] - goal[1])


path = astar_search(
    start_node=(0, 0),
    goal_node=(9, 9),
    get_neighbors_func=neighbors,
    heuristic_func=heuristic,
)
# path is a list of (row, col) tuples from start to goal, or None if unreachable

get_neighbors_func must return an iterable of (neighbor_node, edge_cost) tuples. heuristic_func must be admissible (never overestimate the true cost to the goal) for A* to return an optimal path.

docs.title: Rate limiting (HTTP 429 / 404)
docs.text:
The Overpass API enforces per-IP rate limits. If a request is rejected, map_data automatically backs off and retries on an alternate endpoint. If you see repeated failures in the log:

  • Wait a few minutes before retrying.
  • Avoid running multiple create_mapdata calls in parallel.
  • Consider hosting a local Overpass API instance for high-volume use.

docs.title: Query timeout (HTTP 504)
docs.text: Overpass imposes a default query timeout. Very large bounding boxes (many kilometers across) may exceed it. Reduce the query area by using a shorter GPX route or decreasing grid_margin in config/planner_defaults.yaml.

docs.title: No features returned
docs.text: If md.footways_list or md.roads_list is empty after run_all(), the bounding box may be in an area with sparse OSM coverage. Verify the coverage on openstreetmap.org before debugging the code.

docs.title: MapData(coords="...", coords_type="file") raises "No points (waypoints, tracks or routes) found"
docs.text: MapData reads <wpt> elements if the file has any, otherwise falls back to <trkpt> (tracks) and then <rtept> (routes). Confirm the file contains at least one of these element types.

docs.title: GraphPlanner.plan() returns None
docs.text:
The start or goal point could not be snapped to the road/footway graph. This happens when:

  • The input waypoints are outside the loaded .mapdata bounding box.
  • The requested highway_types (such as ["footway"]) do not include ways that reach both endpoints.
  • The two endpoints are in disconnected graph components.

Try widening the highway_types list to include "road" or check the map in the viewer to confirm that ways connect the two points.

docs.title: ReplanPath.replan() returns None
docs.text:
ReplanPath.replan() returns None and sets failure_reason:

  • start_blocked / goal_blocked: the start or goal lies inside an obstacle with no free cell within 2 m. Move the point or reduce inflate_obstacles.
  • no_path: No collision-free path exists between waypoints given the current obstacle inflation. Try reducing inflate_obstacles (for example from 0.25 to 0.1), adjusting cell_size, or verifying in the viewer that barrier polygons do not completely block the route.
  • cancelled: The planning request was cancelled via cancel_replan_backend() or an action goal cancellation.

docs.title: Flask server fails to start
docs.text:
• Check that port 5000 is not already in use: lsof -i :5000.
  • If you see ImportError: cannot import name 'rclpy', you are running the viewer from within a Python environment where ROS 2 packages are not sourced. The viewer itself does not require ROS 2 for Viewer and Planner modes. Run the viewer directly:
map_data_viewer --data-dir /path/to/data

docs.title: Viewer shows a blank map
docs.text: The Leaflet tile layer requires internet access to load the OpenStreetMap basemap. The vector overlays (roads, footways, barriers) are served locally and will still appear. If the background is blank but features are visible, the tile server is unreachable from your network.

docs.title: Annotations not saving
docs.text: Annotation files are written to <mapdata_filename>.annotations.json next to the .mapdata file. If that directory is read-only (such as inside a ROS 2 install prefix), saving fails. Run the viewer with --data-dir set to a writable directory, or copy the .mapdata file to a writable location first.

docs.title: create_mapdata not found
docs.text:
The command is installed with the package. Standalone, uv sync or pip install -e . puts it on your PATH. In a ROS 2 workspace, create the workspace symlink for map_data_interfaces and build with colcon:

bash scripts/setup_ws.sh
colcon build --packages-up-to map_data
source install/setup.bash

After sourcing, run ros2 run map_data create_mapdata ....

docs.title: osm_cloud does not publish
docs.text:
1. Check that a .mapdata file path is provided via the mapdata_file parameter or launch argument. If no input file is given, osm_cloud logs an error and idles.
  2. Verify the placement frames are available in /tf_static. The node transforms the point cloud into local_frame. Until that transform is available (utm -> local_frame for transform_mode: tf, or earth_frame -> local_frame for geodetic), the node logs Failed to get ... transform and publishes nothing. It picks up the transform as soon as it arrives on /tf_static.
  3. Confirm the grid topic (osm_grid or grid) is present using ros2 topic list.

docs.title: osm_cloud publishes an empty cloud
docs.text:
A Fixposition unit publishes FP_ECEF -> FP_ENU0 as all zeros until it has a fusion fix. In transform_mode: geodetic, an all-zero transform puts the origin at the center of the Earth (-6378 km altitude), collapsing the map into a meter-wide box.

The node rejects all-zero transforms, waits for a valid transform on /tf_static, and logs an error without publishing if the grid is empty while the map contains ways. If you see transform warnings, ensure the GNSS/INS unit has achieved a valid RTK/fusion fix.

docs.title: MapData.load() raises ValueError or JSONDecodeError
docs.text: The file may be truncated or in an unsupported format such as pickle (not valid UTF-8 JSON, raising ValueError). Pickle files are not supported; regenerate the map with create_mapdata -d -f <file>.gpx.

docs.title: UTM zone boundary warning
docs.text: If the log prints Waypoints span multiple UTM zones (...), the map's bounding box crosses a UTM zone boundary. Path planning will still work, but geometry accuracy degrades near the boundary because all features are projected into a single UTM zone. For affected areas, consider splitting the route into segments that stay within one zone.

docs.title: General usage
docs.text:
This page covers the core CLI tools and ROS 2 nodes for parsing, inspecting, and publishing map data.

ROS 2 requirement

ROS 2 is required for osm_cloud and route_planner. The create_mapdata CLI, map_data_info, the MapData class, path planning modules, and the interactive viewer (except the Tracker mode) work standalone.

docs.title: What gets downloaded
docs.text:
When create_mapdata (or MapData.run_all()) is called, a single Overpass API union query is sent covering the bounding box of the GPX waypoints:

[out:json][timeout:170];way(bbox)->.w;(.w; .w >; .w <; node(bbox););out;

This retrieves:

  • Every OSM way intersecting the bounding box.
  • All constituent nodes of those ways.
  • Relations that reference those ways.
  • Standalone nodes inside the bounding box.

The downloaded data is filtered and classified into roads_list, footways_list, and barriers_list according to the tag values in the CSV files in parameters/. Ways and nodes whose tags do not match any configured category are discarded during parsing.

docs.title: Bounding box calculation
docs.text: The query bounding box is derived from the minimum and maximum UTM coordinates of the GPX waypoints, expanded outward in all directions by grid_margin (default 150 m in config/planner_defaults.yaml). The four corner coordinates are converted to WGS-84 latitude/longitude to form the Overpass query bounding box [min_lat, min_long, max_lat, max_long].

docs.title: Inspecting a .mapdata file
docs.text:
map_data_info prints statistics about a .mapdata file — feature counts, total footway distance, covered area, UTM zone, and any stored annotations.

map_data_info coords.mapdata

Example output:

========================================
MAP DATA STATISTICS: coords.mapdata
========================================
Source:      File: coords.gpx
UTM Zone:    33U
Bounds X:    [458200.0, 458900.0]
Bounds Y:    [5550100.0, 5550700.0]
Total Area:  420,000 m²
----------------------------------------
Roads:       12
Footways:    47
Barriers:    83
Total Footway Distance: 4823.6 m
Annotations: 3 (manual edits)
========================================

map_data_info is available after installing the package (standalone pip install -e ., uv sync, or colcon build).

With --validate, the tool checks the file for structural issues instead of printing statistics: missing metadata fields, ways without geometry, duplicate way IDs, nodes missing from the node cache, and disconnected footway networks. It exits non-zero when issues are found, so it can be used as a pre-flight check in scripts:

map_data_info coords.mapdata --validate

docs.title: Parsing and creating files
docs.text: create_mapdata -d builds a .mapdata file from a .gpx file. Without -d it loads the .mapdata file of the same name and saves it again (current file format); it does not reclassify the ways, so tag CSV edits need a new download.

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text: Flag Default Description -h, --help Show help message and exit -f FILE, --file FILE buchlovice.gpx GPX file (a path, or a name in the package's data/ directory or the bundled demo/). Without -d, its .mapdata sibling is re-saved -d, --download false Download fresh data from OSM within the waypoint bounds and parse it --cache false Use the local OSM response cache (30-day expiry)

docs.title: OSM caching
docs.text: Downloaded OSM responses are cached locally keyed by query hash (which embeds the bounding box). If --cache is active and a cache entry exists matching the query within 30 days (OSM_CACHE_MAX_AGE = 30 days), create_mapdata reuses the cached response without querying Overpass again.

docs.title: Output file location
docs.text:
When saving, create_mapdata writes the .mapdata file next to the input GPX file, replacing the .gpx extension with .mapdata.

Download and parse OSM data for a GPX file:

create_mapdata -d -f coords.gpx
# or, in a sourced ROS 2 workspace:
ros2 run map_data create_mapdata -d -f coords.gpx

Rebuild after editing the tag CSVs (--cache skips the download when the cached response is still valid):

create_mapdata -d -f coords.gpx --cache

docs.title: Publishing a point cloud of footways, roads, and intersections
docs.text:
osm_cloud is a ROS 2 node that publishes a sensor_msgs/PointCloud2 on the configured grid topic (osm_grid via launch, or grid on the node) with a cost-aware grid around traversable ways, and optionally publishes intersections as a geometry_msgs/PoseArray and visualization_msgs/MarkerArray.

When started without an input file (mapdata_file or gpx_file), osm_cloud logs an error and idles rather than crashing, preventing a tight restart loop under launch respawn. Runtime parameter changes via ROS 2 parameters are validated before applying; invalid changes are rejected (SetParametersResult(successful=False)).

docs.title: ROS 2 parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description mapdata_file "" Absolute path to a .mapdata file gpx_file "" Absolute path to a .gpx file (used when mapdata_file is empty) grid_topic grid Topic name for the published point cloud (osm_grid in osm_cloud.launch.py) intersections_topic intersections Topic name for intersection poses (PoseArray) intersection_markers_topic intersection_markers Topic name for intersection markers (MarkerArray) local_frame map TF frame the grid and intersections are published in (FP_ENU0 in osm_grid.yaml) utm_frame utm TF frame name for UTM coordinates (transform_mode tf or auto) earth_frame FP_ECEF ECEF TF frame used by transform_mode: geodetic transform_mode tf Placement mode: tf looks up utm_frame -> local_frame on /tf_static; auto calculates the local frame at the map center and broadcasts the static transform; geodetic converts UTM -> lat/lon -> ECEF and applies earth_frame -> local_frame from /tf_static (exact for GNSS/INS stacks; default in osm_grid.yaml) annotations auto Annotation store merged into mapdata_file: auto = <map>.annotations.json next to it, none = unedited map, or a file path exclude_highway ["steps"] highway= tag values dropped from the map (non-routable, so they receive no intersection rings) traversability_file "" Tag rule file deciding which ways are traversable ("" = package default config/traversability.yaml). Traversability rules warning. Must match route_planner's file highway_types ["footway"] Way types the grid is drawn from: footway, road, or both. Must match route_planner's highway_types save_mapdata false Save generated mapdata when loading from a .gpx max_path_dist 1.0 Maximum distance (m) from way centerlines at which grid cells receive a cost neighbor_cost linear Cost falloff for cells near ways: linear, quadratic, or zero grid_res 0.25 Grid resolution / point spacing (m) grid_max [0.0, 0.0] Upper bounds of the local-frame grid (m); [0, 0] enables auto-calculation grid_min [0.0, 0.0] Lower bounds of the local-frame grid (m); [0, 0] enables auto-calculation publish_intersections false Whether to publish footway intersections (true in osm_grid.yaml) republish_period 0.0 Periodic re-publish interval (s); 0.0 publishes once (latched) and on changes

docs.title: Static transform placement
docs.text: osm_cloud listens to /tf_static for its placement transform rather than subscribing to the high-rate /tf stream. When the placement transform changes (for example when a GNSS/INS driver restarts with a new ENU0 origin), the grid and intersections are rebuilt and re-published automatically. In geodetic mode, all-zero transforms (such as an uninitialized fusion fix) are rejected and waited out.

docs.title: Launching
docs.text:
Run the node via its launch file:

ros2 launch map_data osm_cloud.launch.py \
    mapdata_file:=/path/to/coords.mapdata \
    grid_topic:=osm_grid
Argument Default Description osm_grid_params osm_grid.yaml Parameter file in config/ (or path) with OSM grid parameters mapdata_path package share data Directory where bare map filenames are resolved mapdata_file "" Map data filename (resolved in mapdata_path or absolute) gpx_file "" GPX fallback filename (resolved in mapdata_path or absolute) grid_topic osm_grid Topic name for the published point cloud local_frame "" Override frame for the grid/intersections (empty = value from osm_grid_params) utm_frame "" Override UTM frame name (empty = from yaml) earth_frame "" Override ECEF frame name in geodetic mode (empty = from yaml) transform_mode "" Override placement mode: tf, auto, or geodetic (empty = from yaml) annotations auto Annotation store merged into the map: auto, none, or file path traversability "" Tag rule file deciding traversable ways (empty = from yaml) highway_types "" Way types drawn into the grid: footway, road, or footway,road (empty = from yaml)

docs.title: Interactive viewer
docs.text:
map_data_viewer launches a local Flask web server with a Leaflet-based map UI. It lets you inspect and edit parsed features, view their OSM tags, draw manual annotations, and plan paths — without needing ROS 2.

Live demo

A read-only demo of the viewer (Buchlovice dataset) runs at https://vras-robotour.github.io/map_data/demo/ — no installation needed. The demo is read-only: editing, OSM fetching, path planning, and tracker telemetry are disabled in static demo mode. Running map_data_viewer locally provides full functionality.

docs.title: Running the viewer
docs.text:
# Sourced ROS 2 workspace:
map_data_viewer

# Explicit data directory and port:
map_data_viewer --data-dir /path/to/data --port 8080

# Standalone Python environment:
python -m map_data.viewer.app --data-dir ./data

Then open http://127.0.0.1:5000 in a browser.

Trusted networks only

By default the viewer has no authentication and its API can read and write files in the data directory. Keep the default --host 127.0.0.1; only bind to other interfaces (such as --host 0.0.0.0) on networks where you trust every machine, and see Deployment security below for options to lock it down further.

docs.title: Command-line flags
docs.text: Flag Default Description --data-dir <path> package data/ folder Directory containing .mapdata and .gpx files --host <address> 127.0.0.1 Address the Flask server binds to --port <port> 5000 Port the Flask server binds to --telemetry-rate <Hz> 2.0 Tracker telemetry broadcast rate in Hz; see Tracker --config <path> package config/tracker.yaml Tracker topics: a ROS 2 parameter file with a map_data_tracker section. See Tracker

docs.title: API error handling and file safety
docs.text:
• JSON error format: All API error responses return JSON {"error": "<message>"} with the corresponding HTTP status code.
  • No file overwriting: Map uploads (/api/upload_mapdata, /api/upload_gpx) and OSM area fetching (/api/fetch_area) never overwrite an existing .mapdata file. If a file with that name already exists in the data directory, a numerical suffix (_1, _2, etc.) is appended automatically.
  • Corrupt annotation store recovery: If an annotation sidecar file (<stem>.annotations.json) cannot be loaded (due to corruption or invalid JSON), it is moved aside to <path>.corrupt-<timestamp> and answered with HTTP 409 Conflict, preserving the damaged file for recovery without losing edits.

docs.title: Deployment security
docs.text:
The viewer binds to 127.0.0.1 (loopback only) by default, rejects file paths that attempt directory traversal outside the data directory, and avoids deserializing untrusted data. When bound to any other address (e.g. --host 0.0.0.0) without MAP_DATA_ACCESS_TOKEN, the viewer uses a token kept in ~/.config/map_data/access_token ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME respected; created with mode 0600 on first start) and logs the http://<host>:<port>/?access_token=<token> URL to open. The token stays the same across restarts; delete the file to issue a new one.

Two environment variables provide access control:

Variable Default Effect MAP_DATA_ACCESS_TOKEN unset: no auth on loopback, the token file otherwise When set, every HTTP request and Socket.IO connection must supply this token, or it is rejected with 401. MAP_DATA_CORS_ORIGINS unset (same-origin only) Controls which origins may open a Socket.IO connection to the server.

MAP_DATA_ACCESS_TOKEN can be supplied in three ways:

  • Header: X-Access-Token: <token> (for automated clients and robots).
  • Query parameter: http://host:5000/?access_token=<token>. The viewer sets the cookie and redirects to the same URL without the token.
  • Cookie: map_data_access_token, set automatically when authenticating via the query parameter above.

CSRF protection: state-changing requests (POST/PUT/DELETE) must carry an X-Requested-With header (any value) or the X-Access-Token header, with or without a token configured; otherwise they are rejected with 403. The viewer's frontend attaches the header automatically; scripts add it, e.g. curl -H 'X-Requested-With: curl'. Uploads are capped at 100 MB, JSON bodies at 10 MB.

MAP_DATA_CORS_ORIGINS sets Socket.IO's allowed origins. Left unset, only the request's own origin is accepted. Set to a comma-separated list of origins or * to widen access.

Example hardened deployment:

export MAP_DATA_ACCESS_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
export MAP_DATA_CORS_ORIGINS=http://192.168.1.50:5000
map_data_viewer --host 0.0.0.0 --data-dir /path/to/data

docs.title: Base layers
docs.text: The layer control (bottom left) switches between OpenStreetMap and Esri satellite imagery; neither needs an API key. The choice is remembered in the browser.

docs.title: Loading map data
docs.text:
The file selector lists the .mapdata files in the data directory; opening one needs no network access except for the base layer tiles.

New maps come from:

  • GPX import (G, or the GPX button): uploads a track, downloads the OSM data around it and saves a new .mapdata (/api/upload_gpx).
  • Fetch area: downloads a drawn box of up to 25 km² in the background (/api/fetch_area).
  • Drag and drop: a .mapdata file is uploaded as is; a .gpx file builds a new map, or in Planner mode loads its points as waypoints.

.gpx files in the data directory are not opened by the viewer.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
The viewer provides three modes via the tabs in the top-right corner:

Mode Description Viewer Inspect features, manage layer visibility, draw annotations, and edit ways. Supports keyboard shortcuts. Planner Design missions and plan paths using graph-based or all-terrain grid algorithms. Tracker Monitor a live robot via ROS 2 telemetry. Requires a running ROS 2 context.

docs.title: Planner
docs.text: The Planner mode lets you design robot missions and compute planned paths directly in the browser, using the same algorithms as the map_data_plan CLI tool.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Switch to PLANNER using the tab in the top-right corner.
  2. Click on the map to place waypoints. Drag any waypoint to adjust it. With Start at robot ticked the first waypoint is the robot itself, so you only click the goals.
  3. Select a planning mode and configure parameters in the sidebar.
  4. Click Replan Path to compute the path between the placed waypoints.
  5. Download the result as a GPX file or send it directly to the robot via Wormhole.

docs.title: Import and export
docs.text:
Button Description Import GPX Load an existing GPX track as the initial set of waypoints Download Export the planned path as a .gpx file Wormhole Send the planned path directly to the robot over the network Delete All Remove all placed waypoints Keep Endpoints Remove intermediate waypoints, keeping only start and end Start at robot Pin the first waypoint to the robot's live position and plan from there

Start at robot

The toggle requires a robot position, staying disabled until the tracker reports one (telemetry arrives in all modes, so the Robot layer does not need to be active). While enabled, waypoint 0 follows the robot and Replan Path refreshes it before planning.

docs.title: Planning mode
docs.text:
Mode Description All terrain — A* Grid-based A* that finds the optimal path while avoiding OSM barriers and manual annotations. Recommended for most off-road scenarios. All terrain — RRT* Sampling-based planner. Suited for large open areas; falls back to Grid A* if no path is found within the iteration budget. Paths only Constrains the route to the OSM road and footway network, including manually annotated paths. Produces on-network routes.

Path priority

OSM ways and annotated paths take priority over obstacles. A path overlapping a barrier polygon is treated as traversable, allowing you to route through obstacles (such as a gate in a fence).

docs.title: Routing options
docs.text:
• Plan on Footways — include pedestrian footways as traversable ways (default: enabled).
  • Plan on Roads — include vehicle roads as traversable ways.

docs.title: Planner parameters
docs.text:
When the viewer runs under ROS 2 and the tracker's planner_node parameter is active (default: /route_planner), initial toggles and parameter values are synchronized from the running /route_planner node's current parameters. In this case, the UI displays "defaults from /route_planner". When running standalone without ROS 2 or when planner_node is set to "", defaults are loaded from config/planner_defaults.yaml.

Parameter Default Description Cell Size (m) 0.25 Grid resolution for all-terrain planning Obstacle Inflation (m) 0.25 Safety buffer added around barrier polygons Simplify Path on Drop vertices whose shortcut stays collision-free (Douglas-Peucker) Smooth Path off Apply gradient-descent smoothing to the planned path Grid Cost Weight 5.0 How strongly the cell cost weighs against path length in all-terrain planning Show Cost Grid off Overlay the traversal cost grid of the current view on the map for debugging

docs.title: Highway costs
docs.text: The Highway Costs button opens a configuration dialog where you can assign base traversal costs (0.0 = preferred, 1.0 = costly) to each OSM highway type and additional penalties per surface material. These costs are taken into account during both Paths only graph planning (where edge costs are weighted by way costs) and all-terrain grid planning.

docs.title: Traversability rules
docs.text:
The Traversability Rules button opens config/traversability.yaml in an editor. See Traversability rules for rule syntax and synchronization requirements with other nodes.

  • Apply checks the rules and applies them for Paths only planning in the current browser session.
  • Save to file writes the edited rules to disk. route_planner picks up the saved file on its next goal; osm_cloud reads the file only at startup and requires a restart.
  • Reload from file discards unsaved edits and reloads the file from disk.
  • Show only plannable ways hides ways that Paths only will not route over (refused by rules, stairs, or unselected way types).

docs.title: Tracker
docs.text:
The Tracker mode provides a real-time view of a robot's position and hardware status. It requires the viewer to be launched inside a sourced ROS 2 workspace so that the TrackerNode can subscribe to the robot's topics.

ROS 2 required

The Tracker tab is only shown when a ROS 2 context is available. Launching the viewer with map_data_viewer inside a sourced workspace is sufficient — no additional nodes need to be started.

docs.title: Robot marker
docs.text: When telemetry is received, a green arrow marker appears on the map at the robot's current position. The marker rotates to the robot's heading (heading_topic, or azimuth_topic when that is empty). The robot marker is visible in all three modes as long as the Robot layer is enabled in the Layers panel.

docs.title: Sidebar controls
docs.text: Control Description Center Robot Pan and zoom the map to the robot's current position Clear Trail Clear the recorded trail (dropped on the tracker node, so it does not reappear with the next fix) Topics… Open the topic configuration dialog Follow Continuously pan the map to keep the robot centered as it moves

docs.title: Status display
docs.text: The sidebar shows live telemetry grouped into three sections. Each row is hidden automatically if the corresponding ROS 2 topic is not configured.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text: Field Description Battery Voltage (V), current (A) and, with battery_state_topic, pack percentage; turns red below battery_low_voltage E-Stop ACTIVE (red) / released from estop_topic Motors Motor enable state (ENABLED / DISABLED) Temp Hottest sensor_msgs/Temperature (name = its frame_id), or controller temperature Motor Error ODrive error code (displayed in hex when non-zero)

docs.title: Localization
docs.text: Field Description Localization GPS fix quality: Fixed (RTK fixed), Float (RTK float), Fix (standalone fix), or No Fix Fix age Seconds since the last fix; displays red STALE after stale_after Speed Current robot speed in m/s (from odometry) Limit Active speed limit value and unit (m/s or %)

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Field Description State commander_state_topic string (crl_commander mode), active Nav2 behavior tree node, or IDLE Follower road_follower state: ROAD or GPS:<reason> Diagnostics OK, or the number of ERROR/WARN statuses and the worst status message Collision Active collision monitor action (STOP, SLOWDOWN, APPROACH, LIMIT); hidden for DO_NOTHING Recovery Active Displayed in red when a recovery behavior is running Teleop Active Displayed in yellow when teleop velocity commands or joystick inputs were received within 2 s

The sidebar also displays the last five speech messages (info / warn / error level) when speech topics are configured.

docs.title: Map layers
docs.text:
All robot geometry is part of the Robot layer; the Tracker sidebar includes a Map legend listing active layers:

Layer Source Style Planned path path_topic or active Nav2 action green dashed polyline Route / waypoint sequence sequence_path_topic (Path, e.g. road_follower's ~/route_path) blue dotted polyline Waypoint window sequence_poses_topic (PoseArray, e.g. /goal_sequence) light-blue polyline Road path road_path_topic (path_centerline prediction) cyan polyline Goal goal_topic orange circle Trail last trail_length fixes of gps_filtered_topic (else gps_fix_topic), spaced by trail_min_step m; no-fix messages are skipped thin green polyline Intersections intersections_topic (PoseArray, from osm_cloud) magenta rings Active intersection active_intersection_topic with intersection_enter_threshold and intersection_exit_threshold colored radius circles

Poses may be stamped in any TF frame. With earth_frame set (such as FP_ECEF), coordinates are transformed via TF into ECEF and converted to exact lat/lon. If earth_frame is empty, coordinates are transformed into utm_frame and converted with the UTM zone of the current fix.

docs.title: ROS 2 topic configuration
docs.text: The TrackerNode subscribes to configurable topics. Set any topic parameter to an empty string ("") to disable the corresponding feature and hide its UI row.

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
Topic configurations are defined in a ROS 2 parameter file under a map_data_tracker section. By default the viewer reads config/tracker.yaml (generic Nav2 topics); --config selects another file, such as config/helhest_jr.yaml:

map_data_viewer --config config/helhest_jr.yaml

The config file is a standard ROS 2 parameter file, so --ros-args --params-file can also be used.

docs.title: Changing topics in the web app
docs.text:
The Topics… dialog in the Tracker sidebar lists all topic settings and frame parameters. Topic fields indicate live publisher status (green = expected type, yellow = different type, grey = not published, hollow = disabled).

  • Apply updates active subscriptions in the running tracker.
  • Save to file applies changes and updates the active configuration YAML file.
  • Reload from file restores settings from the configuration file on disk.

docs.title: Tracker parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Default topic Description earth_frame "" ECEF TF frame for exact coordinate conversion (FP_ECEF); empty = UTM fallback utm_frame utm UTM TF frame used when earth_frame is empty tf_static_only true Read frames from /tf_static only; set false if frames are published on dynamic /tf gps_fix_topic /gps/fix Raw GPS fix (sensor_msgs/NavSatFix) gps_filtered_topic /gps/filtered EKF-fused GPS position (sensor_msgs/NavSatFix) heading_topic / heading_type "" / imu Heading source: imu (Imu), yaw_vector3 (Vector3Stamped), odometry (Odometry) azimuth_topic /gps/azimuth_imu Legacy IMU heading topic, used when heading_topic is empty odom_topic /odom_2d Odometry for speed display (nav_msgs/Odometry) battery_state_topic "" sensor_msgs/BatteryState (voltage, current, percentage) battery_low_voltage 22.0 Voltage below which the battery indicator turns red bus_voltage_topic /bus_voltage Battery voltage (std_msgs/Float32) bus_current_topic /bus_current Battery current (std_msgs/Float32) temperature_topic "" sensor_msgs/Temperature messages, one row per frame_id teensy_temp_topic /teensy_temp Controller temperature (std_msgs/Float32) odrv_error_topic /odrv_error ODrive error code (std_msgs/UInt64) motors_enabled_topic /motors_enabled Motor enable state (std_msgs/Bool) estop_topic "" Emergency stop state (std_msgs/Bool) diagnostics_topic "" diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray summary commander_state_topic "" Navigation state string (std_msgs/String) follower_state_topic "" Road follower state string (std_msgs/String, latched) bt_log_topic /behavior_tree_log Nav2 behavior tree log (nav2_msgs/BehaviorTreeLog) speed_limit_topic /speed_limit Active speed limit (nav2_msgs/SpeedLimit) collision_monitor_state_topic /collision_monitor_state Collision monitor state (nav2_msgs/CollisionMonitorState) recovery_heartbeat_topic /recovery/heartbeat Recovery behavior heartbeat (std_msgs/Header) teleop_topic /cmd_vel_teleop Teleop velocity command (geometry_msgs/TwistStamped) joy_topic "" Joystick (sensor_msgs/Joy); any input indicates active teleoperation speak_info_topic /speak/info Info speech messages (std_msgs/String) speak_warn_topic /speak/warn Warning speech messages (std_msgs/String) speak_error_topic /speak/err Error speech messages (std_msgs/String) path_topic /path Planned path for map overlay (nav_msgs/Path) goal_topic "" Current navigation goal (geometry_msgs/PoseStamped, latched) sequence_path_topic "" Route sequence being followed (nav_msgs/Path, latched) sequence_poses_topic "" Waypoint window poses (geometry_msgs/PoseArray, latched) road_path_topic "" Visual road path prediction (nav_msgs/Path) intersections_topic "" Intersections (geometry_msgs/PoseArray, latched) active_intersection_topic "" Active intersection (geometry_msgs/PoseStamped, latched) intersection_enter_threshold / intersection_exit_threshold 5.0 / 6.0 Radii drawn around active intersection (m) trail_length / trail_min_step 500 / 0.5 Robot trail size (points) and step distance (m) stale_after 3.0 Fix age threshold (s) after which position is marked stale planner_node /route_planner Node name whose ROS 2 parameters seed Planner toggles ("" disables syncing) nav_through_poses_feedback_topic /navigate_through_poses/_action/feedback Nav2 NavigateThroughPoses feedback topic reporting current waypoint index (nav2_msgs/action/NavigateThroughPoses_Feedback) follow_gps_waypoints_feedback_topic /follow_gps_waypoints/_action/feedback Nav2 FollowGPSWaypoints feedback topic reporting current waypoint index (nav2_msgs/action/FollowGPSWaypoints_Feedback) follow_waypoints_feedback_topic /follow_waypoints/_action/feedback Nav2 FollowWaypoints feedback topic reporting current waypoint index (nav2_msgs/action/FollowWaypoints_Feedback)

Telemetry is broadcast to the browser over WebSocket at 2 Hz by default, configurable via map_data_viewer --telemetry-rate <Hz>. A message goes out only when something changed; the paths, intersections and waypoints only when they changed, and the trail as the fixes added since the previous message. A browser receives the full state when it connects.

WebSocket needs simple-websocket

Without the simple-websocket Python package the browser falls back to HTTP long-polling, one request per message; the viewer logs a warning at startup. pip and uv sync install it, but rosdep has no key for it: on a ROS install add it with pip install simple-websocket (or apt install python3-simple-websocket where the distribution packages it).

docs.title: Viewer
docs.text: The Viewer mode is the default mode of the interactive viewer. It lets you inspect and edit parsed map features, manage layer visibility, and draw manual annotations.

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text: Tool Shortcut Action VIEW v Inspect map features. Click any object to view its OSM tags and properties in the sidebar EDIT e Select and edit existing ways, nodes, and custom annotations + OBS a Draw rectangles, polygons, or circles to add manual obstacle annotations + PATH p Draw custom paths or footways as line annotations. Intersections with other ways form crossroads DEL d Remove objects and custom annotations by clicking on them FETCH f Draw a bounding box to download and parse a new OSM area (up to 25 km²) GPX g Upload a .gpx file to create a new map from a GPS track CLEAR Clear currently loaded map data

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
Keyboard shortcuts operate when not typing into input fields or modals (and mutating actions are disabled in the read-only demo):

Key Action v Switch to View mode e Switch to Edit mode a Add obstacle annotation mode p Add path annotation mode d Delete mode f Fetch OSM area mode g Open GPX file picker n Toggle display of way vertices (in View mode) h Hide or unhide currently selected way (in View mode) Escape Deselect current selection, or return to View mode Delete / Backspace Delete selected annotation (Edit mode), or selected node/way (View mode) Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z Undo last change Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y / Cmd+Shift+Z Redo last undone change

docs.title: Layers panel
docs.text:
The sidebar Layers panel toggles visibility for each feature category:

Layer Color Description Roads Dark grey Vehicle roads from OSM Footways Yellow Pedestrian paths Barriers Red Untraversable features (walls, buildings, fences, water) Crossroads Purple Detected footway intersection points Annotations Orange Manually drawn obstacles and paths Waypoints Blue GPX waypoints from the loaded track Robot Green Live robot position (visible when ROS 2 is available)

A base-layer switcher in the bottom-left corner of the map toggles between standard OpenStreetMap tiles and Satellite imagery (Esri World Imagery). The choice is preserved across sessions.

docs.title: Properties panel
docs.text: Clicking any feature in VIEW mode opens its properties in the sidebar, displaying its OSM tags, category, and geometry. When inspecting individual nodes, copy buttons next to latitude and longitude copy coordinates to the clipboard.

docs.title: Annotation panels
docs.text:
Three collapsible panels track manual edits:

  • Annotations — list of drawn obstacles and paths. Revert buttons restore individual geometries.
  • Changes — features modified since load (tag edits, node moves, splits, additions, deletions). Each entry supports revert; Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo edits sequentially.
  • Hidden — features hidden from the map via the context menu or h key.

docs.title: Exporting edited map data
docs.text:
• Export button: Downloads the fully merged map (with all annotations, node moves, splits, and deletions applied) as a downloadable <stem>.exported.mapdata file. It does not overwrite the source .mapdata file on disk.
  • GeoJSON button: Downloads the merged map as a .geojson file for inspection in GIS tools (such as QGIS).

Incremental edits are automatically saved to <stem>.annotations.json in the data directory.

docs.title: Programmatic annotations
docs.text:
map_data.edits.annotation_store opens a store for editing and writes it back atomically (see Data formats for the schema). Its lock is per process, so do not edit a map the viewer is editing at the same time.

import uuid

from map_data.annotations import annotation_path_for
from map_data.edits import annotation_store

with annotation_store(str(annotation_path_for("coords.mapdata"))) as store:
    store.setdefault("annotations", []).append(
        {
            "id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "type": "obstacle",
            # WGS-84 [lon, lat]
            "geometry": {
                "type": "Polygon",
                "coordinates": [
                    [[14.5678, 50.1234], [14.5680, 50.1234], [14.5680, 50.1236], [14.5678, 50.1234]]
                ],
            },
            "properties": {},
        }
    )

The viewer, map_data_plan, route_planner and osm_cloud merge the store when they load the map.

docs.title: Annotations and edits
docs.text:
Load a map the way the viewer shows it: with its annotation store merged and the traversability rules applied.

from map_data.annotations import load_mapdata_with_annotations

md, store = load_mapdata_with_annotations("my_area.mapdata")

docs.title: Merging a store
docs.text:
Apply a viewer annotation store to a :class:~map_data.map_data.MapData.

The viewer keeps every user edit of a map (deleted ways/nodes, splits, moved nodes, tag overrides, drawn paths and obstacles) in <stem>.annotations.json next to the .mapdata file. Merging it here, outside the web app, lets scripts, map_data_plan and the ROS nodes use the map the viewer shows. :func:load_mapdata_with_annotations is the one-call entry point and :func:apply_store the merge itself.

docs.title: load_mapdata_with_annotations(mapdata_path, annotations_path=None, exclude_highway=NON_ROUTABLE_HIGHWAY_VALUES, traversability=None)
docs.text:
Load a .mapdata file and merge its annotation store.

docs.title: Route planning
docs.text:
plan_route is the entry point the viewer, map_data_plan and route_planner share: graph or grid planning, request validation, waypoint spacing.

from map_data.annotations import load_mapdata_with_annotations
from map_data.pathsolver.route import RoutePlanningError, plan_route

md, _ = load_mapdata_with_annotations("my_area.mapdata")
try:
    result = plan_route(
        md, [(50.1050, 14.4220), (50.1072, 14.4280)], algorithm="graph", spacing=3.0
    )
except RoutePlanningError as e:
    print(e.reason, e.message)
else:
    print(f"{result.length_m:.0f} m, {len(result.latlon)} waypoints")

Plan a route through lat/lon waypoints on a :class:~map_data.map_data.MapData.

This is the headless core of the viewer's Planner screen (POST /api/create_replan): the same graph ("Paths only") and grid ("All terrain") planners, the same parameters, but callable from a script, the map_data_plan CLI or the route_planner ROS action server. The viewer route delegates to :func:plan_route so both stay in sync.

Failures are reported through :class:RoutePlanningError with a machine readable reason instead of a bare None:

too_few_points fewer than two waypoints (after adding the robot position); snap_too_far a waypoint is farther than max_snap_distance from every allowed way (graph planner); unreachable the waypoints lie on disconnected parts of the network (graph planner); no_path the grid planner found no path; start_blocked / goal_blocked a grid leg starts or ends inside an obstacle, with no free cell within :data:~map_data.pathsolver.replan.SNAP_RADIUS_M; cancelled the grid planner was cancelled through its transfer_id; start_outside_map / goal_outside_map the start or goal lies too far outside the map's area (wrong map file?); grid_too_large the requested grid would exceed max_grid_cells cells; route_too_long the route would have more than :data:MAX_ROUTE_POINTS vertices; bad_parameter an unknown algorithm / sub_algorithm, cell_size not finite and above zero, inflate_obstacles negative or not finite, or spacing not finite.

docs.title: plan_route(md, points_latlon, *, algorithm=GRAPH_ALGORITHM, sub_algorithm=None, highway_types=None, max_snap_distance=DEFAULT_MAX_SNAP_DISTANCE, spacing=0.0, cell_size=None, inflate_obstacles=None, simplify_path=None, smooth_path=None, grid_cost_weight=None, highway_costs=None, surface_costs=None, transfer_id=None, max_grid_cells=MAX_GRID_CELLS, planner=None, keep_start=False, keep_goal=False, exclude_highway=NON_ROUTABLE_HIGHWAY_VALUES, traversability=None, outside_map_tolerance=OUTSIDE_MAP_TOLERANCE_M)
docs.text:
Plan a route through points_latlon ([(lat, lon), ...], at least two).

algorithm="graph" routes along the allowed ways only (the viewer's Paths only); "astar"/"rrt" run the grid planner over the cost grid built from the map (All terrain). sub_algorithm picks the grid search ("astar"/"rrt"); None derives it from algorithm. Any other value fails with bad_parameter.

spacing > 0 resamples the result so waypoints are at most that far apart (a waypoint follower wants a few metres; below :data:MIN_SPACING_M fails with bad_parameter). changed and snap_distances are computed before resampling.

planner lets a caller reuse a prebuilt :class:GraphPlanner for md (building the graph costs ~0.3 s, planning on it ~1 ms); it must have been built for the same highway_types and max_snap_distance.

keep_start makes the graph route begin at the first waypoint verbatim rather than at its projection onto the network — for planning from the robot's own position, which is off the network by definition. It has no effect on the grid planners, which already start at the requested point.

keep_goal does the same at the other end: the route ends at the last requested coordinate instead of at its projection, so a goal off the mapped network is actually reached. The off-network leg is resampled by spacing like the rest of the route.

exclude_highway is the highway tag values the graph planner never routes over (stairs by default), and traversability the tag rules that decide the same question from the map's own tags (None = the package's config/traversability.yaml); both are ignored when planner is given, which brings its own.

highway_costs/surface_costs price the highway/surface tags for both planners: the grid planner's cells and the graph planner's edge weights (length * (1 + cost)). None takes config/planner_defaults.yaml, as does None for cell_size, inflate_obstacles, simplify_path, smooth_path and grid_cost_weight (see :func:~map_data.pathsolver.replan.grid_defaults).

A first or last point more than outside_map_tolerance metres outside the map's area fails with start_outside_map / goal_outside_map (see :func:check_in_map).

Raises :class:RoutePlanningError on failure.

A max_snap_distance above the default (or NaN) also takes the default.

docs.text:
A* planner over an undirected graph of a map's footways and/or roads, in UTM.

Annotation ways (negative ids) are spliced in by projecting their loose ends onto the nearest edge. Walkable areas (closed area=yes or multipolygon ways) can be crossed: A* may hop between any two of an area's entries (see :mod:map_data.pathsolver.walkable_area), and a waypoint inside an area is not snapped to its rim.

docs.title: edge_factor(way)
docs.text:
Weight multiplier of way's edges: 1 + way cost + rule cost.

The highway/surface cost comes from the shared tables (:func:~map_data.pathsolver.way_cost.way_cost, the grid planner's own prices), the extra from a cost: in the traversability rules. Never below 1, which keeps the straight-line A* heuristic admissible.

docs.title: Walkable areas
docs.text:
Open walkable areas (pedestrian squares) for the graph planner.

A pedestrian square is mapped as a closed area=yes way, i.e. by its outline only. Routed as a chain of nodes like any other way, it makes a route walk the rim of the square instead of crossing it. :class:WalkableArea keeps the polygon and lets the planner cross it: between two of its entries (network nodes on, inside or within :data:ENTRY_TOLERANCE of the area) it prices the shortest path that stays inside the polygon, holes included.

Such a path bends only at reflex corners of the outline and at hole vertices, so a visibility graph over the entries and those corners is enough. It is built on first use and kept with the area; the planner's global adjacency gains no edges.

docs.title: Way costs
docs.text:
How expensive a way is to drive on, from its highway and surface tags.

Both planners charge the same price for the same way: the grid planner (:class:~map_data.pathsolver.grid_constructor.PathGrid) lowers a cell's cost towards :func:way_cost of the nearest way, and the graph planner (:class:~map_data.pathsolver.graph_planner.GraphPlanner) weighs an edge length * (1 + way_cost). The tables live in config/planner_defaults.yaml (highway_costs, surface_costs, path_cost_cap), so a route that prefers asphalt to gravel is a config change, not a code change.

Which ways are drivable at all is a separate question, answered from the tags by :mod:map_data.traversability; a rule there may add an extra cost on top of the tables for something they do not know about (informal=yes).

docs.title: ReplanPath
docs.text:
Grid planning (Grid A or RRT) over a box around the waypoints. plan_route builds one per request; use it directly to plan on a grid of your own.

import numpy as np
from map_data.map_data import MapData
from map_data.pathsolver.replan import ReplanPath
from map_data.utils.parsing import ways_to_shapely

md = MapData.load("my_area.mapdata")
replanner = ReplanPath(
    ways_to_shapely(md.barriers_list), low=(md.min_x, md.min_y), high=(md.max_x, md.max_y)
)
replanner.fill_grid(md, highway_types=["footway"])

start = np.array([md.min_x + 10, md.min_y + 10])
goal = np.array([md.max_x - 10, md.max_y - 10])
path = replanner.replan(np.array([start, goal]), algorithm="astar")
if path is None:
    print(replanner.failure_reason)

Constructor keywords left None (cell_size, inflate_obstacles, simplify_path, smooth_path, grid_cost_weight, highway_costs, surface_costs) take the values of config/planner_defaults.yaml; see Planner configuration. The resolved tables are the instance attributes highway_costs, surface_costs, path_cost_cap and default_off_path_cost.

replan() returns the path, or None with failure_reason set to no_path, start_blocked, goal_blocked or cancelled. To cancel a run from another thread, construct it with a unique transfer_id and call cancel_replan_backend(transfer_id).

docs.text:
Which ways the robot may drive on, from config/traversability.yaml. See Traversability rules for the file format.

Decide from OSM tags which ways the robot may drive on.

Turns a way's tags into drive here / never drive here / drive here reluctantly, from the operator-edited rule file config/traversability.yaml.

The rules are used through :class:TraversabilityRules by:

  • :func:~map_data.annotations.load_mapdata_with_annotations drops the non-traversable ways from the map at load time, so the route planner, the intersection rings and the osm_cloud cost cloud all describe the same network;
  • :class:~map_data.pathsolver.graph_planner.GraphPlanner filters them again (for callers that pass a raw map) and adds a rule's optional cost to the highway/surface cost of :mod:map_data.pathsolver.way_cost when it weighs the way's edges, so a "possible but unpleasant" way is taken only when the alternative is much longer;
  • the route_planner and osm_cloud nodes and the map_data_plan CLI pass the file the operator picked.

The file format is documented in config/traversability.yaml itself and in docs/planning.md. This module imports nothing from ROS.

docs.title: Viewer REST API
docs.text:
Internal API

The viewer's JavaScript is the client of this API. It is documented for tooling that talks to a running viewer.

All endpoints are served by map_data_viewer. Handlers live in map_data.viewer.routes, one module per section: files, annotations, ways (ways and nodes), planning, sharing (goal QR codes and wormhole); shared helpers in common. The tracker endpoints are in map_data.viewer.tracker_routes.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Errors are JSON {"error": "<message>"} with the HTTP status, for every endpoint.
  • 413: a JSON body over 10 MB, or any request over 100 MB (the multipart uploads).
  • Every response carries X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'.
  • 409: the file's annotation store exists but is not a readable JSON object. It is moved aside to <store>.corrupt-<timestamp> and never overwritten; reload to continue with an empty store.
  • file is a .mapdata name in the data directory. A name that resolves outside it is 400, a missing file 404.
  • way_id is an OSM way ID or a split segment "<id>:<index>".
  • Edits are written to <stem>.annotations.json under a per-file lock; the .mapdata file is never modified. See Data formats.

docs.title: GET /api/files
docs.text: {"mapdata": [name, ...], "gpx": [name, ...]}, sorted. Empty lists when the data directory does not exist.

docs.title: GET /api/mapdata?file=<name>
docs.text:
The map with its way edits and tag overrides applied, as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Drawn annotations are not included (the client draws them from /api/annotations). The response has an ETag; a matching If-None-Match gets 304.

Way feature properties:

Property Type Description id int or str Way ID, "<id>:<index>" for split segments category str road, footway, barrier or crossroad tags object OSM tags with overrides applied in_out str "outer" / "inner" for multipolygon members, else "" is_node bool true for a barrier made from a single obstacle node

Geometry is Polygon, MultiPolygon or LineString; roads and footways are buffered polygons. Waypoints are Point features with category: "waypoint" and index.

docs.title: POST /api/fetch_area
docs.text:
Starts a background download and parse of an OSM area; returns {"task_id": "<uuid4>"} at once.

{
  "min_lat": 50.07, "min_lon": 14.40, "max_lat": 50.09, "max_lon": 14.43,
  "name": "my_area",
  "grid_margin": 150, "obstacle_radius": 2.0,
  "buffer_widths": {"road": 7, "footway": 3, "barrier": 2}
}
  • The box plus its grid_margin must be at most 25 km² (MAX_FETCH_AREA_KM2).
  • name is sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_-]. An existing map, or a leftover <name>.annotations.json, is never overwritten: the map is saved as <name>_1.mapdata, <name>_2.mapdata, ...
  • grid_margin, obstacle_radius, buffer_widths are optional; defaults from config/planner_defaults.yaml.

400: missing or invalid field, box too large, empty name. 429: two Overpass fetches (fetch_area or upload_gpx) already running.

docs.title: GET /api/fetch_area/<task_id>
docs.text:
The task record, polled by the client:

status Other fields pending, querying, parsing detail (progress text) done result: {"filename", "roads", "footways", "barriers", "crossroads"} failed error

A finished task is kept for 60 s after it is first polled. 404: unknown or evicted task.

docs.title: POST /api/upload_gpx
docs.text:
Builds a map around an uploaded GPX track, synchronously. multipart/form-data:

Field Required Description file yes The GPX file name no Output stem (default: the upload's stem), sanitized as for fetch_area options no JSON object with grid_margin, obstacle_radius, buffer_widths

Saved under the next free name, as for fetch_area; the Overpass cache is written next to it. Returns {"filename", "roads", "footways", "barriers", "crossroads"}.

400: bad file, name or options, or the area (with margin) exceeds 25 km². 429: two Overpass fetches already running. 503: Overpass unreachable. 500: parsing failed.

docs.title: POST /api/upload_mapdata
docs.text:
Saves an uploaded .mapdata file (multipart/form-data, field file) under the next free name. It is checked with MapData.load under a temporary name first, so an unreadable file never appears. Returns {"filename": "<saved name>"}.

400: missing file, wrong extension or unreadable map.

docs.title: GET /api/export?file=<name>
docs.text: Downloads <stem>.exported.mapdata: the map with every annotation applied, as .mapdata JSON. Nothing is written to the data directory.

The segment after the split starts at a new synthetic copy of the node, so the ends move independently and the planner does not route across the split. Returns {"success": true, "segments": [...]}. 400: node_id is not an interior node of the edited way. 404: unknown way.

Records node positions for the way; every segment shares them.

{"nodes": [{"id": 111, "lat": 50.0715, "lon": 14.4015}], "category": "footway", "label": "..."}

All nodes are validated before anything is written; each must be on the edited way (a split end counts, a way without nodes takes its own ID). 204. 400: invalid position or a node not on the way. 404: unknown way.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text: The map_data package has four layers: data ingestion, representation, planning and visualization.

docs.title: MapData
docs.text:
MapData (map_data/map_data.py) is the central data class. It takes a .gpx file (waypoints or a track) or a UTM coordinate array, downloads the OSM data around it and parses it into Way lists.

Bounding box. The waypoints' axis-aligned UTM bounding box, expanded by grid_margin (default 150 m, config/planner_defaults.yaml) on every side. MapData(..., grid_margin=...) overrides it.

Overpass query. run_queries() sends one union query for the box: every way, its nodes, the relations that reference it, and every node. Nothing is filtered server-side; run_parse() classifies client-side. OverpassClient (map_data/utils/overpass.py) rotates endpoints, retries, and rejects error bodies.

Parsing. run_parse():

  1. parse_osm_ways builds a Way per OSM way (closed ways become polygons, except linear barriers such as fences and walls).
  2. parse_osm_rels merges multipolygon relation members into rings, stamps the relation's tags onto untagged outers and subtracts inner rings.
  3. parse_osm_nodes turns standalone obstacle nodes into circles.
  4. separate_ways sorts ways into roads, footways and barriers (see Tag configuration).
  5. parse_intersections adds a crossroad wherever a footway/road node branches.

Attributes after parsing:

Attribute Type Description roads_list list[Way] Non-footway highway ways, buffered to 7 m wide polygons footways_list list[Way] Footway-class highway ways, buffered to 3 m wide polygons barriers_list list[Way] Barrier polygons, buffered barrier lines and obstacle circles crossroads_list list[Way] Junction circles of radius CROSSROAD_RADIUS (1.5 m) nodes_cache dict[int, dict] OSM node ID → {lat, lon, tags} zone_number, zone_letter int, str UTM zone of the input waypoints waypoints np.ndarray (N, 2) UTM input waypoints min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y float UTM bounding box including grid_margin

OSM cache. The raw Overpass response is saved as <stem>.osm_cache.json next to the source GPX. It is reused when the hash of the query (which contains the bounding box) matches and it is younger than 30 days (OSM_CACHE_MAX_AGE). run_queries() uses it by default (the viewer's fetch and GPX upload); run_all() bypasses it, and create_mapdata uses it only with --cache.

Serialization. MapData.save() writes JSON (.mapdata) atomically; MapData.load() reads it and recomputes the node-based crossroads. See Data formats.

Traversability. MapData.apply_traversability(rules) removes the roads and footways the traversability rules refuse and recomputes the crossroads. It runs at load time (load_mapdata_with_annotations), not at parse time, so the .mapdata file keeps the full OSM classification.

docs.title: Way objects
docs.text:
Every OSM feature is a Way (map_data/utils/way.py):

  • id: OSM way or node ID; negative or string IDs for merged relation rings, viewer-drawn annotations and split segments;
  • is_area: True when line is a polygon;
  • nodes: ordered OSM node IDs;
  • tags: OSM tags;
  • line: Shapely geometry in UTM. Roads, footways and open barrier lines are buffered to Polygons during parsing; MapData.centre_line(way) recovers a footway's centerline;
  • in_out: "outer" or "inner" for multipolygon members, else "".

docs.title: Annotations and edits
docs.text:
Viewer edits live in <stem>.annotations.json next to the .mapdata file, which is never modified.

  • map_data/edits.py: the annotation store (load, quarantine of an unreadable store, the locked annotation_store() context manager) and the way-edit pipeline that rebuilds a way's nodes and line from deleted, moved, added and split nodes.
  • map_data/annotations.py: apply_store(md, store) merges a store into a MapData (way edits, tag overrides, drawn paths and obstacles, join_ways). load_mapdata_with_annotations() loads a map, merges its store and applies the traversability rules in one call; edit_mapdata() does the same for an already loaded map. The viewer, map_data_plan, route_planner and osm_cloud all use it, so they see the same map.

join_ways gives ways that meet without a shared node ID a junction node: a drawn path's loose end or a moved end node within JOIN_DISTANCE_M (5 m) of another way, and every crossing of a drawn path.

docs.title: Pathsolvers
docs.text: map_data/pathsolver/route.py is the shared entry point: plan_route(md, points_latlon, algorithm=...) validates the request, runs the graph or grid planner and returns a RouteResult, or raises RoutePlanningError with a machine-readable reason. The viewer, map_data_plan and route_planner all call it.

docs.title: GraphPlanner
docs.text:
map_data/pathsolver/graph_planner.py

A* over the OSM way network (footway and/or road). Ways connect by shared node ID. An edge weighs length × (1 + way cost + rule cost) (see Planner configuration); reported lengths stay geometric. Waypoints snap to the nearest edge through an STRtree; a waypoint farther than max_snap_distance fails with snap_too_far. Open pedestrian areas (WalkableArea, walkable_area.py) are crossed through a visibility graph instead of walked around their rim.

docs.title: ReplanPath
docs.text:
map_data/pathsolver/replan.py

Cost-grid planning over a box around the waypoints:

Module Class / function Responsibility grid_constructor.py PathGrid Cost raster at cell_size; cells near a way take its cost, obstacle cells are inf grid_astar.py grid_astar 8-connected A* on the raster rrt_star.py RRTStar Sampling planner with informed sampling and an adaptive rewiring radius smoothing.py smooth_path Gradient-descent smoothing with collision checks way_cost.py way_cost, load_cost_tables highway/surface cost shared with GraphPlanner

replan() plans each leg between consecutive waypoints. A straight leg that hits no obstacle is kept. Otherwise blocked ends are moved to the nearest free cell within SNAP_RADIUS_M (2 m), and the leg fails fast when start and goal lie in disconnected free regions. RRT falls back to A when it finds no path. The result is then smoothed (optional) and simplified. On failure it returns None and sets failure_reason (no_path, start_blocked, goal_blocked, cancelled).

Defaults come from grid_defaults(); see Planner configuration.

docs.title: Viewer
docs.text:
map_data/viewer/ is a single-page Flask + Leaflet application.

Back-end:

Module Responsibility app.py App factory, Socket.IO, CLI (map_data_viewer), optional ROS 2 thread routes/ The viewer blueprint: files (page, file list, map, fetch, uploads, export), annotations, ways (way and node edits), planning (planner defaults, traversability, cost grid, replan), sharing (goal QR codes, wormhole), common (JSON errors, path helpers, way resolution, validators, get_merged_mapdata) helpers.py GeoJSON conversion cache.py Read caches keyed on file signature and annotation-store digest ros_node.py TrackerNode, the Tracker's ROS 2 subscriber tracker_routes.py, tracker_config.py Tracker settings API and its parameter file

Every error is JSON {"error": message}; see Viewer REST API.

Front-end modes (static/js/):

Mode Entry point Purpose Viewer ui_handlers.js, layers.js, draw_handlers.js Inspect, edit, annotate and search OSM features Planner planner_mode.js Waypoints, route planning, GPX download, goal QR codes Tracker tracker_mode.js Live robot telemetry over Socket.IO

docs.title: Executables
docs.text:
Executable File Kind Purpose create_mapdata map_data/create_mapdata.py CLI Build a .mapdata from a GPX file map_data_info map_data/info.py CLI Statistics and validation of a .mapdata file map_data_plan map_data/plan_route_cli.py CLI Plan a route offline (plan_route) map_data_viewer map_data/viewer/app.py CLI, optional ROS 2 Web viewer; with ROS 2 also runs TrackerNode osm_cloud map_data/osm_cloud.py ROS 2 node Publishes the way network as a cost-grid PointCloud2, intersections as PoseArray and markers route_planner map_data/route_planner.py ROS 2 node PlanRoute action server on ~/plan_route; publishes the route latched

The PlanRoute action is defined in the nested map_data_interfaces/ package.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
1. Create the map: create_mapdata -f <file>.gpx -d, or Fetch area / GPX upload in the viewer, writes <name>.mapdata.
  2. Inspect and annotate: the viewer renders the map; edits go to <name>.annotations.json.
  3. Plan: the viewer's Planner, map_data_plan or a PlanRoute goal to route_planner load the map with its annotations and traversability rules and call plan_route.
  4. Drive: osm_cloud publishes the same map for the navigation stack; the viewer's Tracker shows the robot and its route.
